3:1.sourceText: Πέτρος δὲ καὶ Ἰωάνης ἀνέβαινον εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν ἐπὶ τὴν ὥραν τῆς προσευχῆς τὴν ἐνάτην.
3:1.targetText: And Peter and John were going up at the same time into the temple, at the hour of the prayer, the ninth [hour],

groups.note: The one printed hour noun is qualified by ninth in the same immediate time expression. English repeats that same hour as [hour] in apposition; both renderings retain one actual source hour identity, without a second written noun.

N1904 places ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό at the end of 2:47 in the adding/saved clause, while pinned TR places the phrase at 3:1. LSV at the same time renders it temporally in this new clause. The cross-reference preserves that changed attachment and temporal rendering; it does not label the N1904 2:47 use inherently temporal or invent a separate time noun.

3:2.sourceText: καί τις ἀνὴρ χωλὸς ἐκ κοιλίας μητρὸς αὐτοῦ ὑπάρχων ἐβαστάζετο, ὃν ἐτίθουν καθ’ ἡμέραν πρὸς τὴν θύραν τοῦ ἱεροῦ τὴν λεγομένην Ὡραίαν τοῦ αἰτεῖν ἐλεημοσύνην παρὰ τῶν εἰσπορευομένων εἰς τὸ ἱερόν·
3:2.targetText: and a certain man, being lame from the womb of his mother, was being carried, whom they were laying every day at the gate of the temple, called Beautiful, to ask a kindness from those entering into the temple,

groups.note: The actual genitive article/asking infinitive supplies the purpose to ask. Its infinitive head remains joined rather than assigning bare to to the article alone.
Actual ἐλεημοσύνη is the alms/charitable-gift noun, rendered a kindness by LSV. This retains the printed noun rather than substituting a generic kindness lemma.

unmappedSource.reason: The repeated attributive article before called is not separately expressed in English.

3:3.targetText: who, having seen Peter and John about to go into the temple, was begging to receive a kindness.

3:4.sourceText: ἀτενίσας δὲ Πέτρος εἰς αὐτὸν σὺν τῷ Ἰωάνῃ εἶπεν Βλέψον εἰς ἡμᾶς.

3:5.targetText: and he was giving heed to them, looking to receive something from them;

groups.note: The article ὁ is used pronominally with δέ to resume the man, rendered he. No separate personal pronoun is printed at that position.

3:6.sourceText: εἶπεν δὲ Πέτρος Ἀργύριον καὶ χρυσίον οὐχ ὑπάρχει μοι· ὃ δὲ ἔχω, τοῦτό σοι δίδωμι· ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τοῦ Ναζωραίου περιπάτει.
3:6.targetText: and Peter said, “I have no silver and gold, but what I have, that I give to you; in the Name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, rise up and be walking.”

groups.note: Actual ὑπάρχει μοι is an existence-plus-dative-possession construction, literally exists to me, rendered I have. Both real words jointly anchor this possession phrase; no ἔχω source verb is invented at the first I have.
The actual article/Nazarene designation is rendered of Nazareth with Jesus Christ, keeping the personal geographic designation rather than inventing a different place noun.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV includes an additional rising imperative and conjunction, corroborated by TR ἔγειραι καί. Pinned N1904 has the one walking imperative without these words.
